social_security.summary: Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits included in federal gross income are subtracted, so Indiana does not tax them.

sources.quote: (8) Subtract an amount equal to the amount of federal Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits included in a taxpayer's federal gross income by Section 86 of the Internal Revenue Code.
Indiana does not tax Social Security and railroad retirement benefits issued by the Railroad Retirement Board.

public_pension.summary: State and local government pensions have no special Indiana deduction and are taxed as part of federal AGI; federal civil service annuitants 62 or older may deduct up to $16,000, reduced by Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement received.
conditions: Federal civil service annuity (not military): deduction up to $16,000 at age 62+ (or surviving spouse), minus Social Security/Tier 1 RR benefits received

sources.quote: (a) In the case of all individuals, "adjusted gross income" (as defined in Section 62 of the Internal Revenue Code), modified as follows:
(B) first sixteen thousand dollars ($16,000), for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2015;
(b) The individual is only entitled to the deduction provided by this section if the individual is at least sixty-two (62) years of age before the end of the taxable year.
If you received a civil service pension (nonmilitary*) and are at least 62 years of age, then you may be eligible for up to a $16,000 deduction.

private_pension.summary: Private pensions, 401(k) and IRA distributions are taxed by Indiana as part of federal adjusted gross income; there is no special deduction.

military_retirement.summary: For 2022 and later, the entire amount of U.S. military retirement income and survivor's benefits included in AGI is deductible.

sources.quote: (iv) For taxable years beginning after 2021, one hundred percent (100%) of the amount of the benefits in excess of six thousand two hundred fifty dollars ($6,250).

The amount of the deduction is the lesser of: (A) the benefits included in the adjusted gross income of the individual or the individual's surviving spouse; or (B) six thousand two hundred fifty dollars ($6,250) plus the following:
For 2022 and later, the deduction is equal to the entire amount of military retirement income and/or survivor’s benefits.

notes: DOR states that the taxable portion of pensions is taxable in Income Tax Information Bulletin #26 and the IT-40 booklet, both PDFs lexflow cannot read here, and no DOR web page saying so was found, so private_pension has a statute source only (Indiana starts from federal AGI and has no general pension deduction). The federal civil service annuity deduction (IC 6-3-2-3.7) is recorded under public_pension conditions because Indiana treats federal civil service differently from state and local pensions, which get no deduction.
